title: Specialists Learn Faster: Knowledge Organization in Pre-training Shapes Knowledge Update Efficiency
abstract: arXiv:2610.13835v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: An ideal (language) model must continually update its knowledge. Existing work largely focuses on making these updates efficient after training. We investigate how the organization of time-varying knowledge during pre-training shapes the efficiency of subsequent updates. Models trained on chronologically ordered knowledge specialize in the most recently encountered knowledge; we call them specialists. In contrast, models trained on the same knowledge in randomly shuffled order perform well across all represented time periods; we call them generalists. Surprisingly, specialists require far fewer update steps than generalists to acquire new knowledge. To explain this advantage, we derive a law from first principles that relates update cost to the model's optimization dynamics and that closely predicts empirical results. translated_title: 专家学得更快：预训练中的知识组织方式决定知识更新效率
translated_abstract: 理想的（语言）模型必须能够持续更新其知识。现有研究主要关注如何在训练完成后使这些更新变得高效。我们研究了预训练期间时变知识的组织方式如何影响后续更新的效率。按时间顺序组织知识进行训练的模型会专精于最近接触到的知识，我们将其称为“专家”（specialists）；相比之下，使用随机打乱顺序训练相同知识的模型在所有呈现的时间段上均表现良好，我们将其称为“通才”（generalists）。令人惊讶的是，专家模型获取新知识所需的更新步骤远少于通才模型。为解释这一优势，我们从第一性原理出发推导出一个定律，该定律将更新成本与模型的优化动力学联系起来，并能很好地预测实验结果。基于这些发现，我们设计了一种预训练数据组织策略，以保留稳定的历史知识……
tldr: 研究发现按时间顺序组织预训练数据所形成的“专家”模型比随机打乱顺序训练的“通才”模型能以更少的更新步骤更高效地获取新知识，并从第一性原理推导出解释该现象的定律，据此设计了保留稳定历史知识的预训练数据组织策略。
en_tdlr: Specialists—models pre-trained on chronologically ordered knowledge—acquire new knowledge with far fewer update steps than generalists trained on shuffled data, a phenomenon explained by a first-principles law linking update cost to optimization dynamics, which guides a pre-training data organization strategy that preserves stable historical knowledge.
